reuse.why: Extends the existing getDateWithSkippedWeekend with a holidays parameter and adds a shared isSkippedDay predicate in shared/schedules.ts, reused by getNextDate and the server date functions.

duplication.why: getUpcomingDates now re-implements the same per-occurrence 'skip daily / move otherwise / filter null' mapping that getDatesInRange has, in a reordered shape, and the '(holidays.length) + 3' look-around constant is restated in several places.

placement.why: The day-skipping rule lives in shared/schedules.ts, where the weekend rule already lived; server code only consumes it.

scope.why: Includes unrelated churn in app.test.ts (import reordering and reformatting of existing getDatesInRange calls).

maintainability.why: The optional holidays parameter defaults to [] so callers that forget it silently ignore holidays: budget/schedule-template.ts still calls getDateWithSkippedWeekend without holidays, so the rule is not applied there.

bypasses_abstraction.where: All weekend handling still goes through getDateWithSkippedWeekend / the new isSkippedDay.

disguised_duplication.where: server/schedules/app.ts getUpcomingDates: its new map (skipWeekend guard, daily-and-skipped -> null, else getDateWithSkippedWeekend, filter null) is the same logic as getDatesInRange's map, reordered rather than shared.

one_place.where: isSkippedDay/getDateWithSkippedWeekend in shared/schedules.ts hold the rule, but holidays must be threaded by each caller and budget/schedule-template.ts (two getDateWithSkippedWeekend calls) is not updated, so that path still treats only weekends as skipped.
